lesson_title: HCF and LCM Without Listing a Single Multiple
hook_text: 180 and 300. HCF and LCM in 20 seconds — no lists, just bricks.
clip_script: Here is the rule, read directly from index form. The HCF takes every prime that appears in BOTH factorisations, each raised to the LOWER of its two powers. Set the anchor pair side by side. 180 is two squared, three squared, five. 300 is two squared, three, five squared. Prime two appears in both: powers two and two, lower is two, take two squared. Prime three appears in both: powers two and one, lower is one, take three. Prime five appears in both: powers one and two, lower is one, take five. HCF equals two squared times three times five, which is four times fifteen: 60.
visual_style: Two columns of coloured prime bricks (blue 2s, green 3s, orange 5s) for 180 and 300; the shared bricks slide together into a 60 tile, then every brick at its tallest stack merges into a 900 banner.
pacing: Build both brick piles quickly, pause on the comparison, two snaps for HCF and LCM.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn when a problem wants the tile and when it wants the taxis.
